units.summary: Pupils trace the history of public health from Roman aqueducts through medieval cesspits to Victorian sewers, evaluating why progress was not linear and how government attitudes shaped change over time.
units.vocab: Aqueduct, Cesspit, Miasma Theory, Cholera, Laissez-faire, Germ Theory, Public Health Act 1848
units.assessment: Extended PEEL paragraphs at the end of each period studied. Unit assessment: "Why did it take so long to clean up Britain?" (extended writing)
units.smsc: Social: Responsibility for community health. Moral: Should governments compel people to change behaviour for the public good? Cultural: How different civilisations approached hygiene.
units.careers: Public Health Officer, Epidemiologist, Archaeologist, Environmental Scientist

units.summary: Pupils explore the power struggles that defined England from the Norman Conquest to the Wars of the Roses, examining how monarchs, the Church, and ordinary people competed for authority and power across the High and Late Middle Ages.
units.vocab: Feudalism, Domesday Book, Magna Carta, Crusade, Black Death, Peasants' Revolt
units.assessment: Formative PEEL paragraphs throughout. Mid-unit assessment: Magna Carta baronial enquiry. Final assessment: 12-mark extended essay — "Explain why the peasants revolted in 1381."
units.smsc: Spiritual: Power and influence of the medieval Church. Social: Feudal hierarchy and peasant resistance. Moral: Is rebellion ever justified?
units.careers: Archivist, Heritage Site Manager, Historian, Lawyer

units.summary: Pupils examine why Europe was not the centre of global power in 1450, how religious conflict triggered exploration, and how early trading encounters escalated into empire and the Transatlantic Slave Trade.
units.vocab: Reformation, Conquistador, Transatlantic Slave Trade, East India Company, Colonisation, Triangular Trade
units.assessment: Formative PEEL paragraphs and source work throughout. Final assessment: "To what extent was greed the main cause of European exploration?"
units.smsc: Moral: Ethics of colonisation, slavery, and cultural destruction. Social: Impact of global trade on indigenous societies. Cultural: Encountering and evaluating diverse civilisations.
units.careers: Museum Curator, International Relations Analyst, Human Rights Lawyer

units.summary: Pupils investigate how industrialisation transformed Britain into the world's first industrial superpower and evaluate the human cost of factory life, urbanisation, and imperial expansion across the globe.
units.vocab: Industrial Revolution, Urbanisation, Child Labour, Imperialism, Chartism, Free Trade, Working Class
units.assessment: Formative source analysis and knowledge checks. Final assessment: "Was the British Empire a force for good or harm?" (extended judgement essay)
units.smsc: Social: Urbanisation, child labour, and inequality. Moral: Was Empire a force for good or exploitation? Cultural: Impact of industrialisation on working-class life and identity.
units.careers: Urban Planner, Economist, Politician, Museum Educator

units.summary: Pupils critically examine the British colonisation of Australia, from the decision to establish a penal colony to the devastating and lasting impact on Indigenous peoples and their enduring resistance.
units.vocab: Terra Nullius, Convict, Indigenous, Dreaming, Dispossession, Penal Colony, First Fleet
units.assessment: Analytical written response: "How significant was the impact of British colonisation on Indigenous Australians?"
units.smsc: Cultural: Respect for Indigenous Australian heritage and traditions. Moral: Legacies of penal transportation and dispossession. Social: Long-term impact of colonialism on First Nations peoples.
units.careers: Anthropologist, Human Rights Advocate, Social Worker, Journalist

units.summary: Pupils analyse the complex web of long and short-term causes of the First World War, including militarism, imperialism, the alliance system, nationalism, and the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
units.vocab: Militarism, Alliance System, Imperialism, Nationalism, Assassination, Schlieffen Plan, Arms Race
units.assessment: Formative source utility tasks throughout. Final assessment: "Was the assassination of Franz Ferdinand the main cause of the First World War?" (16-mark essay)
units.smsc: Moral: Duty, sacrifice, and the ethics of warfare. Social: Impact of war on local communities — Stubbington's "Lost Generation". Cultural: War poetry, propaganda, and remembrance.

units.summary: Pupils investigate the lived experience of the trenches, challenge the "Lions led by Donkeys" debate, uncover the forgotten contributions of Empire troops, and evaluate the consequences of the Treaty of Versailles.
units.vocab: Trench Warfare, Attrition, Shell Shock, Somme, Treaty of Versailles, Conscription, Empire Troops
units.assessment: Final assessment: "How far do you agree that the Treaty of Versailles made a second world war inevitable?" (16-mark interpretations essay)
units.smsc: Moral: The "Lions led by Donkeys" debate. Social: Forgotten contributions of Empire soldiers. Cultural: Remembrance and collective memory.
units.careers: Military Historian, Diplomat, Archivist, Documentary Maker

units.summary: Pupils study the deep roots of antisemitism, the escalating persecution under Nazi rule, and the systematic genocide of the Holocaust contextualised by the Second World War and Operation Barbarossa, developing an understanding of moral responsibility and remembrance.
units.vocab: Antisemitism, Pogrom, Nuremberg Laws, Kristallnacht, Ghetto, Einsatzgruppen, Final Solution
units.assessment: Analytical essay: "How did ordinary people become perpetrators of genocide?" Pupil Voice reflection exercise on Holocaust Memorial Day.
units.smsc: Moral: Profound reflection on genocide, prejudice, and human rights. Social: Bystander responsibility and moral courage. Spiritual: The Holocaust's impact on faith and human meaning.
units.careers: Human Rights Advocate, Educator, Ethics Adviser, Museum Curator

units.summary: Pupils explore how the wartime alliance between the USA and USSR collapsed into ideological rivalry, examining key flashpoints from the Berlin Blockade to the Cuban Missile Crisis and the fall of the Berlin Wall.
units.vocab: Capitalism, Communism, Iron Curtain, Proxy War, Nuclear Deterrence, Berlin Wall, Détente
units.assessment: Formative knowledge checks and source tasks. Final assessment: "Who was more to blame for the Cold War — the USA or the USSR?" (extended judgement essay)
units.smsc: Moral: Ethics of nuclear deterrence and proxy wars. Social: Ideological division of the world. Cultural: The propaganda war, the space race, and cultural competition.
units.careers: Political Scientist, Intelligence Analyst, Diplomat, Journalist

units.summary: Pupils evaluate the transformation of Britain from 1945 to 2000 — from the creation of the Welfare State and the NHS to the Windrush generation and the ongoing struggle for equality and civil rights.
units.vocab: Welfare State, NHS, Windrush, Civil Rights, Feminist Movement, Deindustrialisation, Multicultural
units.assessment: Final assessment: "How much did Britain change between 1945 and 2000?" — a thematic extended writing response.
units.smsc: Social: Creation of the Welfare State, Windrush, and multiculturalism. Moral: Equality, protest, and civil rights in post-war Britain. Cultural: Immigration and the evolution of British identity.
units.careers: Sociologist, Public Policy Analyst, Civil Servant, Teacher

units.shortTitle: Paper 2: Conflict in the Middle East (1945–1995)
units.summary: Pupils study the origins and escalation of the Arab-Israeli conflict from the end of the British Mandate to the Oslo Accords, analysing the wars of 1948, 1956, 1967, and 1973 and the search for peace.
units.vocab: Zionism, Mandate, Balfour Declaration, Intifada, PLO, Occupied Territories, Oslo Accords
units.assessment: Edexcel Paper 2 exam practice throughout: 4-mark consequence questions, 8-mark narratives, and 16-mark importance essays. End of unit mock under timed conditions.
units.smsc: Moral: Ethics of partition, displacement, and military conflict. Social: Impact of prolonged war on civilian populations and refugees. Cultural: Religious and national identity in the Middle East.
units.careers: Diplomat, Foreign Correspondent, International Aid Worker, Political Analyst

units.summary: Pupils analyse the rise and fall of the Weimar Republic, Hitler's consolidation of power, and the structures of the Nazi totalitarian state, developing skills to evaluate sources and historical interpretations.
units.vocab: Hyperinflation, Reichstag, Enabling Act, Gestapo, Propaganda, Kristallnacht, Autarky
units.assessment: Edexcel Paper 3 exam practice: 4-mark inference, 12-mark utility, and 20-mark interpretations essays. End of unit timed mock assessment.
units.smsc: Moral: How democracy can be destroyed from within. Social: Impact of propaganda and totalitarianism on everyday society. Cultural: Weimar cultural revolution versus Nazi cultural control.
units.careers: Political Analyst, Human Rights Lawyer, Journalist, Educator

units.summary: Pupils study how ideas about the cause, prevention, and treatment of disease changed from the medieval period to the present day, and how the extreme conditions of the Western Front drove surgical innovation. Supported by the biannual GCSE Ypres Battlefield Tour (Years 10–11) investigating historic British sector dressing stations, casualty evacuation chains, and the Menin Gate.
units.vocab: Four Humours, Miasma, Vaccination, Germ Theory, Penicillin, Blood Transfusion, RAMC
units.assessment: Edexcel Paper 1 exam practice throughout. End of unit timed mock: 16-mark essay — "The most important factor in the development of medicine was science and technology. How far do you agree?"
units.smsc: Social: Government responsibility for public health then and now. Moral: Ethics of medical experimentation, vaccination, and battlefield triage. Cultural: Collective memory, the Ypres Salient, and commemoration at the Menin Gate.
units.careers: Doctor, Medical Researcher, Public Health Policy Maker, Pharmacist

units.summary: Pupils examine the political, religious, and social challenges Elizabeth I faced — from the religious settlement and Catholic plots to the threat of the Spanish Armada — and evaluate her success as a monarch.
units.vocab: Religious Settlement, Puritan, Recusant, Mary Queen of Scots, Spanish Armada, Privateer, Poor Law
units.assessment: Edexcel Paper 2 exam practice: 4-mark consequence, 8-mark narrative, and 16-mark importance essays. End of unit timed mock.
units.smsc: Spiritual: Religious conflict and the Elizabethan Religious Settlement. Cultural: Elizabethan theatre, maritime exploration, and court culture. Social: Poverty, vagrancy, and Elizabethan social control.

units.summary: Targeted revision across all three papers using past papers, walking-talking mocks, and bespoke exam technique workshops.
units.assessment: Full timed mocks across Paper 1, 2, and 3. Walking-talking mock sessions and targeted one-to-one intervention.
units.smsc: Resilience, self-regulation, growth mindset, and managing exam pressure.
units.careers: All career pathways — analytical thinking, written communication, and structured argument are transferable skills for any profession.
